text: 17. QA Handbook

This section is the single source of truth for how CoLab is tested. It documents the **real, committed test harness** (Playwright end-to-end specs and Node `node:test` integration tests), explains how to run it, and then provides a large, actionable catalog of concrete test cases grouped by category (Smoke, Regression, Performance, Accessibility, Security, Cross-Browser, Mobile/Responsive, Meeting, and Call). Every claim about the existing automated suite is grounded in the files under `e2e/`, `playwright.config.ts`, and `backend/app/test/`. Where a test category is aspirational rather than already automated, that is stated plainly so the next engineer never mistakes a manual checklist for a green CI lane.

title: What is and is not automated today
text: The committed automated suite is intentionally small: three Playwright e2e spec files (smoke, responsive, accessibility) run across three device profiles, plus two backend `node:test` integration files (calls signalling, identity). Everything else in this section — performance budgets, deep security cases, cross-browser matrices, full meeting/call media validation — is a **specified test plan** that a human or future automation executes. Do not assume a case is green in CI just because it appears in a table here.
17.1 Testing Philosophy and the Quality Gate

CoLab follows a *thin-but-real* testing strategy. Rather than mocking the backend, the end-to-end tests boot the **actual** Express backend and Next.js frontend against a real MySQL database and sign in like a real user. This catches integration defects (auth envelope shape, socket handshakes, same-origin proxy rewrites, hydration races) that a mock-heavy suite would miss. The trade-off is that the suite needs a running MySQL instance and is slower; it is therefore deliberately narrow, asserting the highest-value invariants (the app shell renders, no horizontal overflow at any width, no serious/critical accessibility violations, call signalling is gated and directional).

In plain language: the tests prove *the app actually starts, looks right on every screen size, lets a user in, and does not leak calls to people who should not be on them*. In engineering language: the suite exercises the real auth flow (`POST /api/auth/login` returning the `{ok,data,error}` envelope), the Socket.IO handshake (`auth:{token}` verified server-side), the LiveKit token-mint IDOR guards, and the responsive CSS `zoom` ramp — all against a live stack.
The master quality gate is the `truth` npm script (aliased as `gate`). It chains every check in order and is the definition of "done" before a release. Any red link stops the chain.

lines: npm run truth   # == npm run gate

text: Note two important facts about this gate. First, `tsc --noEmit` is a hard gate even though `next.config.js` sets `eslint.ignoreDuringBuilds:true` — ESLint warnings do not block the build, but a TypeScript type error does. Second, `security` and `secrets` are supply-chain and secret-leak guards (npm-audit high-severity and secretlint), not application test cases; they belong to the gate but are out of scope for the functional test catalogs below.

title: Single browser engine — "cross-browser" is not yet automated
text: All three Playwright projects (`desktop`, `tablet`, `mobile`) use Chromium device descriptors (`Desktop Chrome`, `iPad (gen 7)`, `iPhone 13`). There is **no Firefox or WebKit/Safari project** in `playwright.config.ts`. The device profiles vary the viewport and touch/pointer affordances, not the rendering engine. The Cross-Browser test catalog in 17.11 is therefore a **manual matrix** until WebKit/Firefox projects are added. Treat Safari/iOS-Safari behaviour (especially `getUserMedia`, `setSinkId`, and `zoom`) as unverified by automation.
17.3 The Playwright E2E Harness in Detail
17.3.1 Configuration

`playwright.config.ts` defines the whole e2e environment. Key settings: `testDir:"./e2e"`, `timeout:90000` (90s per test — generous because it waits on a real backend), `retries:1`, `workers:1` (serial; the tests share one database and one authenticated account so parallelism would cause cross-talk), `baseURL:"http://localhost:3002"` (the frontend dev port), and `trace:"on-first-retry"` (a Playwright trace is captured only when a test is retried, keeping artifacts small).

The config also *owns the stack lifecycle* via `webServer`. It starts `npm run dev:backend` and waits for `http://localhost:4000/api/health`, and starts `npm run dev:frontend` and waits for `http://localhost:3002`. `reuseExistingServer:true` means if you already have the stack running locally, Playwright attaches to it instead of spawning a duplicate. The backend is pinned to `DATABASE_URL=mysql://colab:colab@localhost:3306/colab`, and `DEMO_MODE` is deleted so the suite runs against the real (non-demo) database profile.

text: 17.3.2 Global setup and the seeded account

`e2e/global-setup.ts` calls `prepareReleaseDatabases()` from `database/src/prepare-release-dbs.ts` before any test runs. That helper runs `migrate(url)` then `seedDemo(db,{usersOnly:true})` against each target database (default `colab` and `colab_demo`), and ensures two fixtures exist: a DM `conv_emily` between `u_you` and `u_emily`, and a channel `conv_general` containing `u_you`, `u_emily`, `u_marcus`, `u_priya`, `u_david`, `u_lena`. This guarantees the login account and at least one conversation always exist, so the smoke and responsive specs are deterministic.

`e2e/_helpers.ts` exports `gotoApp(page)`, the login routine every spec calls. It navigates to `/`, fills the email (`you@colab.app`) and password (`demo1234`), and — critically — wraps the fill in an `expect(...).toPass()` retry loop. The comment documents the reason: the login form is a hydrated React controlled component, and a `fill()` that lands before hydration completes is reset to `""` by React's first render, which then submits an empty email and fails with "Invalid email or password." The retry re-fills until the values stick (hydration done) before clicking `button.btn-p`. It then waits for the `/api/auth/login` 200 response and for `#rail` to be attached and visible. **Any new e2e test must reuse `gotoApp` rather than re-implementing login**, or it will be flaky on the slower tablet/mobile projects against `next dev`.

title: Hydration-race pattern is reusable
text: The `expect(async () => { fill; assert value stuck }).toPass()` pattern in `_helpers.ts` is the canonical fix for any controlled-input flakiness against `next dev`. If you add tests that type into other controlled fields (search, composer, settings), wrap the fill the same way.
17.3.3 The committed e2e specs

`smoke.spec.ts` (2 tests): asserts the authenticated shell renders (`#rail`, `#vdash`, and a `.dash2-greet` containing the greeting text matching `/Good/`), and that the document has no horizontal overflow (`scrollWidth - innerWidth <= 2`).

`responsive.spec.ts` (5 tests): desktop shows `#sidebar` and `#main` together; mobile collapses to a single pane and the `.mobile-back` button returns to the sidebar; desktop hover tooltips are not clipped off-screen (`boundingBox().x/y >= 0`); **no horizontal overflow on any rail module** (walks Dashboard, Messages, Calls, Contacts, Calendar, Activity, Tasks, Reminders, Files and asserts `scrollWidth <= clientWidth+2` per view); and **no horizontal overflow across the width spectrum** (sweeps 320, 360, 390, 480, 600, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440, 1920, 2560, 3440 px and asserts no overflow at each). The desktop-only and mobile-only tests are scoped via `test.skip(project.name !== ...)`.

`accessibility.spec.ts` (1 test): runs `new AxeBuilder({page}).analyze()` on the home view and asserts there are **zero** violations of impact `critical` or `serious`. Violations of impact `moderate` or `minor` are explicitly tolerated by this assertion — which is exactly where the known color-contrast gap lives (see 17.10).
17.3.4 Backend integration tests (node:test)

`backend/app/test/calls-signalling.test.ts` is an in-process integration test. It sets test secrets (`AUTH_JWT_SECRET`, `LIVEKIT_API_KEY/SECRET`, `LIVEKIT_WS_URL`, `CALL_MISSED_MS=1500`), migrates+seeds the database, creates an Express app, attaches Socket.IO, and listens on an ephemeral port. If MySQL is unavailable the DB-backed cases **skip** (via the `dbTest` wrapper) while the pure token-minting case still runs. It asserts: `roomToken` mints a LiveKit-valid JWT whose `sub` is `u_alice` or `u_alice__<uuid>` with a `video` grant for the right room and `canPublish:true`; the `/api/calls/token` endpoint returns 401 without auth; group tokens require conversation membership (non-member gets **403**, IDOR closed); 1:1 tokens require being a participant in that specific call (a third user gets **403**); the ringing flow `request -> incoming -> accept` works and is membership-gated (a fresh non-connected user calling anyone gets a `call:error` with code **403**); and `CALL_INCOMING` reaches the correct peer in **both** directions (the directional-ringing regression).

`backend/app/test/identity.test.ts` unit-tests `otherMemberId([members], self)` from the frontend `lib/identity.ts`. It guards the directional ringing fix: the caller's `peerId` must resolve to the *other* member relative to the real self id in both directions and independent of member order; a hardcoded non-member self id (`u_you`) reproduces the original "calls yourself" bug; and empty/single-member/missing inputs return `null`.
17.4 How to Run the Tests

items: Ensure MySQL is up and reachable at `mysql://colab:colab@localhost:3306/colab` (the e2e config and the backend integration test both default to this URL). Without it, e2e fails to boot and DB-backed `node:test` cases skip.
First time only, install Playwright browsers: `npx playwright install`.
Run the full e2e suite across all three device projects: `npm run test:e2e`.
Run only the accessibility lane: `npm run a11y`.
Run the backend integration/unit tests: `npm run test:unit`.
Run the entire release gate: `npm run truth` (a.k.a. `npm run gate`).

title: The e2e suite mutates a real database
text: `global-setup` migrates and seeds the `colab` (and `colab_demo`) databases and the calls integration test deletes rows from the `calls` table for the test users between subtests. Never point `DATABASE_URL` at a production database when running tests. Use a local/disposable MySQL. The `migrate-db.ts` script is guarded to refuse non-loopback hosts for exactly this reason.
17.5 Test Case Catalogs — How to Read Them

Each catalog below is a table with columns **ID, Area, Steps, Expected result, Priority**. IDs are stable handles (e.g. `SMK-01`) so defects and CI lanes can reference them. Priority is P1 (release-blocking), P2 (important), or P3 (nice-to-have). Where a case is already covered by a committed automated test, the Steps or Expected column names the spec/file so you know it is green, not just planned. Cases without such a reference are manual or future-automation.

Regression tests lock in behaviours that have broken before and must never break again. Several map directly to documented incidents and to the committed integration tests. There is no automated performance suite committed today. `npm run scan` only prints a command to point `react-scan` at the running dev server, and `npm run analyze` builds with `@next/bundle-analyzer`. title: Why the render-storm case is P1
text: Per the architecture, `CoLabV1.tsx` is a ~9,000-line god-component holding nearly all app state; every socket event can re-render the whole tree unless children are memo'd and props are passed via refs. PRF-01 guards that the memoization (ChatView is React.memo'd, props stabilized via refs) is intact — a regression here degrades the entire app, not one screen.

text: 17.10 Known Accessibility Gap — Color Contrast

title: Color-contrast violations are NOT caught by the green a11y lane
text: `accessibility.spec.ts` asserts only that there are no `serious`/`critical` axe violations. Color-contrast findings frequently surface at `moderate` impact, and the assertion deliberately filters those out (`impact === 'critical' || impact === 'serious'`). As a result the automated lane can be green while real AA contrast failures exist — especially on the accent-on-dark theme variants (oled/midnight/forest) where accent backgrounds are clamped. This is a deferred, design-owned item: the contrast remediation across all six themes is pending, and verification UI work was prioritized behind it.

Action for QA: when running A11Y-03, do **not** rely on the e2e lane. Run an explicit axe color-contrast audit (or a manual contrast-checker) against each of the six themes — light, dark, oled, midnight, slate, forest — and each accent. File contrast failures against the design system tokens in `styles/v1.css` (`:root` grayscale ramp and `--ac*` accent set), not against individual screens, because the fix belongs at the token layer. Business impact: failing AA contrast blocks enterprise procurement that requires a VPAT/WCAG-AA conformance statement, so this gap is a sales-relevant risk, not a cosmetic one.
17.11 Cross-Browser Tests

As noted in 17.2, the automated suite runs only on Chromium. Cross-browser coverage is therefore a manual matrix today, prioritized by where browsers genuinely diverge for CoLab: media capture (`getUserMedia`), audio output routing (`setSinkId`), the CSS `zoom` property (non-standard, Chromium/WebKit support it; Firefox historically did not), screen share (`getDisplayMedia` with system audio), and IndexedDB (E2EE key storage). Each case should be run on the latest stable of each engine.

text: 17.13 Security Tests

Security cases combine the automated IDOR/membership guards (from `calls-signalling.test.ts`) with a manual plan covering authentication, authorization, rate limiting, headers, and the optional DM E2EE. The supply-chain (`audit-ci`) and secret-scan (`secretlint`) lanes run in the gate but are not application test cases. Authorization in CoLab is predominantly **resource-membership based** (e.g. `db.conversations.isMember`), not global-role based, so the highest-value security tests are membership/IDOR checks on every resource route.

title: Socket handshake does not re-check the blocklist
text: SEC-02 is HTTP-scoped. The Socket.IO handshake verifies the JWT signature but does **not** consult the token blocklist (only the HTTP `authMiddleware` does). A token revoked at logout remains usable on an already-open or freshly-opened socket until it expires (7-day default TTL). When testing revocation, verify the HTTP path is blocked and note the socket path as a known limitation rather than a passing case.
17.14 Call Tests (1:1 and Group)

Calls are the highest-risk subsystem because they cross the media plane (LiveKit SFU + coturn TURN) and depend on the deployment's TLS and firewall posture. The signalling layer is partly automated (`calls-signalling.test.ts`), but **media flow (audio/video actually traversing ICE/DTLS) requires an HTTPS deployment with TURN and cannot be validated by the in-process tests** — those only prove tokens mint and ringing routes correctly. Use `lib/callDiagnostics.ts` / `CallDebugPanel.tsx` (enable via `localStorage colab_call_debug=1` or `?calldebug=1`) to inspect the selected ICE candidate pair (host/srflx/relay), protocol, RTT, and whether TURN was used.

title: Media-plane cases need a real deployment
text: CALL-07, CALL-08, CALL-13, CALL-16, CALL-17, and CALL-18 cannot be proven by the committed automated tests — they exercise actual WebRTC media over ICE/DTLS, which requires a secure (HTTPS/WSS) deployment, a reachable LiveKit SFU, and a correctly firewalled coturn. The signalling tests prove only that tokens and ringing are correct. Always run the media-plane cases on a staging deployment that mirrors production network topology (including the regional SFU if Mumbai media relocation is active), with `colab_call_debug=1` enabled, before signing off a release.
17.15 Meeting Tests

Meetings reuse the LiveKit media stack but add scheduling, recurrence, a lobby/lock/eject access model (where the meeting UUID is the access credential and `meetingService.enterRoom` is the real gate), host/co-host controls, persisted in-meeting chat, hand-raise, reactions, and recording. As with calls, signalling/authorization is testable in-process but real media and recording require a deployment (and server-side egress requires the egress container, which is not provisioned in current deployments — recording is PARTIAL).

text: 17.16 Defect Triage and Reporting

When a test fails, capture the evidence the suite already produces before re-running. Playwright writes a trace on first retry (`trace:"on-first-retry"`); open it with `npx playwright show-trace`. For runtime/app issues, the in-app DiagnosticsPanel (open via `Ctrl+Alt+D`, `?diag=1`, or `window.__colabDiag()`) renders health chips and a copyable build report from the `lib/logger.ts` ring buffer; `window.colabLogs.copy()` dumps the structured log. For call/meeting media issues, attach the `[CALLDIAG]` console trail and the CallDebugPanel readout (candidate-pair type, protocol, RTT, packet loss, TURN used/advertised).

items: Reproduce against the local stack at the documented DB URL; confirm it is not a stale-data artifact (re-run global-setup).
Capture the Playwright trace (retry artifact) and/or the DiagnosticsPanel report and CALLDIAG trail.
Record the test ID (e.g. CALL-08), device project (desktop/tablet/mobile), browser engine, and deployment tier (local/teams/live).
Classify: P1 release-blocker, P2 important, P3 nice-to-have, mapping to the priority in the case tables.
For media-plane failures, state explicitly whether signalling passed (token + ring) and only media failed — that points at network/TLS/TURN, not app code.

text: 17.17 Coverage Gaps and Roadmap

To keep this handbook honest, the following are the explicit gaps between the case catalogs above and what is actually automated today. Each is a concrete next step for the test suite, not a hidden weakness.

rows: Add `webkit` and `firefox` Playwright projects; install engines
Add an explicit per-theme contrast audit; fix at the `--ac*`/grayscale token layer
Add a render-count assertion harness for PRF-01 and a pagination perf budget
Add a deployment smoke that joins a real LiveKit room with fake devices and asserts a connected pair
Provision the egress container in staging; convert MTG-16 from 503-expected to a real recording case
Add a blocklist check to the socket auth middleware and a SEC-02 socket variant
Computed but not wired to UI
Wire safety-number verification UI, then add an A11Y/SEC case for it

title: Definition of release-ready
text: A release is QA-signed when: `npm run truth` is fully green; the media-plane call and meeting cases (CALL-07/08, MTG-05/06/07) pass on a staging deployment that mirrors production network topology; the per-theme color-contrast audit has no new regressions; and any open P1 defect has either a fix or an explicit, written waiver from the product owner. P2/P3 items may ship with tracked tickets.
